themes: Longitudinal trajectory of plasma p-tau217 in early Alzheimer's disease
Comparison of p-tau217 and NfL for tracking disease progression
Association of plasma p-tau217 with cognitive decline and brain atrophy
one_line: Plasma p-tau217 levels increase longitudinally in preclinical and prodromal Alzheimer's disease and correlate with cognitive decline and brain atrophy, suggesting utility as a minimally invasive biomarker for monitoring disease progression.
summary: This study investigated the longitudinal changes of plasma p-tau217 in 150 cognitively unimpaired individuals and 100 patients with mild cognitive impairment from the Swedish BioFINDER cohort. Over a median follow-up of 4.3 years, plasma p-tau217 levels increased significantly in participants with preclinical (amyloid-β positive, cognitively unimpaired) and prodromal (amyloid-β positive, mild cognitive impairment) Alzheimer's disease. In contrast, p-tau217 remained stable in amyloid-β negative individuals and those who did not progress to Alzheimer's disease dementia. The longitudinal increases in p-tau217 were significantly correlated with worsening cognitive scores (MMSE and mPACC) and accelerated brain atrophy in the temporal cortex and hippocampus. Plasma neurofilament light (NfL), a general marker of neurodegeneration, did not show an Alzheimer's disease-specific increase over time. The findings indicate that plasma p-tau217 is a dynamic biomarker during early Alzheimer's disease and could be valuable for monitoring disease progression and evaluating therapies in clinical trials.

key_claims.claim: Plasma p-tau217 increases over time in preclinical and prodromal Alzheimer’s disease.
key_claims.evidence: Preclinical (Aβ+ CU) and prodromal (Aβ+ MCI) AD had accelerated p-tau217 compared to Aβ- CU (β = 0.56, P < 0.001) and Aβ- MCI (β = 0.67, P < 0.001).

key_claims.claim: Plasma p-tau217 does not change in Aβ- participants or MCI patients who do not convert to AD dementia.
key_claims.evidence: P-tau217 remained stable over time in the Aβ− MCI group (β = 0.12, P = 0.39) and in MCI patients who did not develop AD dementia (β = 0.053, P = 0.68).

key_claims.claim: Longitudinal increases in p-tau217 correlate with worsening of cognition.
key_claims.evidence: For each standard deviation higher slope of p-tau217, the decline in MMSE accelerated by β = −0.15 points (P < 0.001) in the overall CU group, and β = −0.35 points (P < 0.001) in overall MCI.
key_claims.location: Results (Longitudinal plasma p-tau217 and longitudinal cognition)

key_claims.claim: Longitudinally increased p-tau217 correlated with accelerated atrophy of temporal cortex and hippocampus.
key_claims.evidence: For each SD higher slope of p-tau217 the thinning of temporal cortex accelerated by β = −0.0057 mm (P < 0.001) per year in the overall CU group. Hippocampal volume atrophy accelerated by β = −7.56 mm3 (P < 0.001).
key_claims.location: Results (Longitudinal plasma p-tau217 and longitudinal atrophy)

limitations: Subgroups were relatively small (e.g. n=49 Aβ+ MCI), lowering power to detect some structural correlations.
Study cohort restricted to Swedish BioFINDER, limiting geographical and ethnic diversity.
